about: One sentence cut in half by a rubric. The priest says the first half still at the altar, having kissed it and bowed his head to the Cross. Then he turns to the people and, finishing the sentence, signs them with the cross — both witnesses print a cross in the text, each in a different place. The rubric insists that he blesses once only, even at solemn Masses. The threefold blessing belongs to a Pontifical Mass. The blessing is not given where Ite, Missa est was not said: after Benedicámus Dómino, nor in Masses for the Dead.

s01.narrative: Then the priest kisses the altar, raises his eyes, extends, lifts and joins his hands, bows his head to the Cross, and says:

s03.narrative: And turned towards the people, blessing once only — even at solemn Masses, for the threefold blessing belongs to a Pontifical Mass — he goes on:

s04.translation: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

s05.narrative: In Masses for the Dead no blessing is given. After Requiéscant in pace the priest says Pláceat tibi, sancta Trínitas, kisses the altar, and reads the Gospel of Saint John.

w001.function: Subjunctive of wish — not “God blesses” but “may God bless”. The subject “Deus” (w004) comes last of all, while the object “vos” (w002) comes second.

w003.function: Agrees with “Deus” (w004), although it stands before it.

w005.function: Nominative, not vocative: it is in apposition to “Deus” (w004). The three Persons are not being called upon here but named — this is the God who blesses.

w009.function: In the 4th declension the nominative and genitive singular are spelled alike. What settles it is the series the word stands in — Pater, Fílius, Spíritus, all in one case.
